chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from al-ʿAbbās, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
I asked him about al-firāʾ, al-sinjāb, al-sammūr, foxes, and the like. He said: There is no harm in praying in it.

key_terms.الثَّعَالِبِ: foxes, whose fur is included in the question
key_terms.السَّمُّورِ: sable or a similar fur-bearing animal mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.السِّنْجَابِ: squirrel fur mentioned specifically among the materials discussed
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the act of worship whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.الْفِرَاءِ: fur garments or pelts being asked about for use in salat
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no objection; an expression indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat in garments made from squirrel, sable, fox, and similar furs?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning salat (prayer) in garments made from certain furs, including al-sinjāb and al-sammūr. The Imam عليه السلام states that there is no objection to performing salat in such materials, making it relevant to discussions of permissible clothing in worship.
